clinical_knowledge.topic: Post-Viral Cough (Acute Bronchitis) evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Post-Viral Cough (Acute Bronchitis) is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes symptomatic care and avoiding unnecessary antibiotics (Choosing Wisely), adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: dry cough for 10 days after cold, normal chest exam

Key HPI features: A 62-year-old female presents to the clinic with dry cough for 10 days after cold, normal chest exam. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
Objective/Exam findings: Normal vital signs, no fever, clear lung fields on auscultation with no wheezes, crackles, or focal findings.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Post-Viral Cough (Acute Bronchitis).
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Pneumonia without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: High fever, focal findings.
management_principles: Plan for Post-Viral Cough: Choosing Wisely: avoid antibiotics
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: Patient presenting with chief complaint of dry cough for 10 days after cold, normal chest exam. HPI: Persistent dry cough for 10 days following an upper respiratory infection, no fever, no shortness of breath.
reference_soap.objective: Normal vital signs, no fever, clear lung fields on auscultation with no wheezes, crackles, or focal findings.
reference_soap.assessment: Post-viral cough (acute bronchitis), given a normal chest exam and absence of fever or focal findings that would suggest pneumonia.
reference_soap.plan: Plan for Post-Viral Cough: Choosing Wisely: avoid antibiotics. Honey, OTC dextromethorphan. Consult specialist if symptoms worsen. Counsel patient.
